page: Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on Microsoft Hyper-V. It is built on an Intel Xeon 8573C x86_64 processor clocked at 4.2 GHz, equipped with 8 physical cores and 16 dedicated vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. The configuration includes 260 MB of L3 cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX matrix extensions. It provides 512 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32 GB per vCPU. Local temporary storage is provisioned via 3,780 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD capacity. There are no discrete GPUs included, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark metrics indicate balanced compute throughput and high in-memory operational capacity. In standard processing suites, the server logged a Geekbench single-core score of 1,714 and a multi-core score of 11,346, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 25,302.46. Memory subsystem testing demonstrated 100.42 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 57.42 GB/sec uncached write bandwidth across large 256 MB blocks, reaching 1,171.61 GB/sec in cached small-block scenarios. In application benchmarks, the instance sustained 21.05 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 21.14 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For CPU-based inference workloads, the Intel AMX instruction support facilitates prompt processing at 107.84 tokens per second on 7B parameter language models.

The constrained vCPU architecture paired with an expansive 512 GB RAM footprint offers cost efficiency for software platforms licensed on a per-core basis that demand massive RAM capacities. Coupled with the 3,780 GB local NVMe SSD, Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v6 is suited for large in-memory caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise relational databases, distributed analytics engines, and data transformation pipelines that require extensive temporary scratch space and high memory bandwidth without necessitating full 64-core compute licensing costs.
description: The Microsoft Azure E64-16ds_v6 is a memory-optimized instance operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The system provides 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, paired with 512 GB of system RAM, yielding a high ratio of 32 GB of memory per vCPU. Hardware features include 260 MB of L3 cache, advanced instruction support for AVX-512 and Intel AMX, and 3,780 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without integrated GPUs. Benchmark evaluations show a PassMark CPU score of 25,302.46, uncached read bandwidth of 100.42 GB/sec, and Redis SET throughput exceeding 21 million operations per second. By constraining vCPU count while retaining the memory allocation of a larger chassis, this server configuration optimizes per-core software licensing costs for memory-bound workloads, large relational databases, in-memory key-value stores, and analytical data caching.
